items.title: Govt to amend two laws to facilitate death registration of missing persons
items.summary: Kathmandu, October 6 The government is preparing to amend two laws to facilitate the registration of deaths of people who went missing in the devastating Bhotekoshi–Trishuli disaster. The amendments will be pursued through a “fast-track” process. items.title: Four districts still have blocked roads as Rasuwa highway stays shut
items.summary: Kathmandu, October 6 Several roads across the country remain fully blocked today as well. Police said roads in Rasuwa, Myagdi, Manang and Nawalparasi East are blocked. According to police, Rasuwa’s main highway remains completely blocked, and the blockage on the Beni–Jomsom road in Myagdi has not been cleared. items.title: Nepal’s disaster panel is debating what to call the Bhotekoshi floods. ‘Himalayan tsunami’ isn’t on the list
items.summary: Prime Minister Balendra Shah used the term at the UN, but experts on the government panel say they are considering other names for the August 26 disaster.

items.title: Nepal scales back flood search as Rs559b reconstruction effort begins
items.summary: The government has suspended search and rescue operations for Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods except in emergencies, directing authorities to accelerate reconstruction and rehabilitation in flood-hit areas.
